title: Chapter 5 – The Integumentary System
notes: Skin has two layers: epidermis (keratinized stratified squamous) and dermis; hypodermis (subcutaneous) is deep but not skin.
Epidermal cell types: keratinocytes, melanocytes, Langerhans (immune), Merkel (tactile).
Thin vs thick skin: thick has stratum lucidum and thicker stratum corneum; no hair.
Epidermal layers (deep→superficial): basale, spinosum, granulosum, lucidum*, corneum.
Dermis layers: papillary (areolar, capillaries, Meissner corpuscles); reticular (dense irregular, Pacinian).
Skin color: melanin (eumelanin/pheomelanin), hemoglobin, carotene.
Hair anatomy: shaft, root, follicle; growth cycles (anagen, catagen, telogen).
Glands: sebaceous (oil), eccrine sweat (thermoregulation), apocrine (axillary/pubic), ceruminous (earwax).
Nails: keratinized plates; protective and functional roles.
Functions: protection, thermoregulation, sensation, excretion/absorption, vitamin D synthesis.
Wound healing: epidermal vs deep (inflammation→migratory→proliferative→maturation).
Development: epidermis (ectoderm), dermis (mesoderm); appendages are epidermal derivatives.
Aging: reduced sweat/sebum, thinner skin, decreased melanocytes, loss of subcutaneous fat.
Skin cancer types: basal cell, squamous cell, malignant melanoma.
ABCDE of melanoma: Asymmetry, Border, Color, Diameter>6mm, Evolving.
Burns: degrees by depth; risks include fluid loss and infection.
Hypodermis anchors skin and stores triglycerides; highly vascular.
Papillary ridges contribute to fingerprints; improved grip.
Sebum lubricates skin/hair and reduces water loss.
Eccrine sweat is watery and aids heat loss by evaporation.
Apocrine sweat contains proteins/lipids; bacterial action causes odor.
Vitamin D synthesis requires UV exposure; supports Ca2+ absorption.
Deep wound healing includes scar formation (fibrosis).

questions.question: Which epidermal layer is present only in thick skin?
questions.explanation: Stratum lucidum appears in thick skin.

questions.question: Eccrine sweat glands function mainly in:
questions.explanation: They cool the body via evaporation.
